condition.narrative: Article IV: Effectiveness - The Recipient has prepared and adopted the Project Operations Manual pursuant to Section I.B.1(a) ofSchedule 2 to this Agreement and in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, A. Institutional and Implementation Arrangements, 1. For the purpose ofensuring the efficient and effective implementation of the Project, the Recipient shall maintain, throughout the period ofimplementation of the Project, Project implementation structures with mandate, resources and composition satisfactory to theAssociation as set out in the Operations Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, A. Institutional and Implementation Arrangements, 2. (a) establish by not laterthan 120 days after the Effective Date and thereafter maintain within its Secretariat throughout the period of implementation ofthe Project, a project implementation unit, chaired by a qualified Project director with qualification, experience and terms ofreference satisfactory to the Association and staffed with competent personnel in adequate numbers and with qualification,experience, and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association (“Project Implementation Unit”), which unit shall be granted thefunctions, decision making-powers and -sufficient resources, as agreed with the Association, for the carrying out of the Project,including its planning, budgeting, technical coordination, implementation supervision, monitoring and evaluation, and environmentaland social aspects;

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, A. Institutional and Implementation Arrangements, 2.(b) establish by no laterthan 120 days after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project, a Projectsteering committee, chaired by SACEP Director General and comprised of, inter alia, Recipient's Director General, head of Chancery,and Project Implementation Unit's Project director, as further detailed in the Operations Manual (the “Project SteeringCommittee”), which committee shall be responsible for providing strategic guidance and oversight for the overall design andimplementation of Project activities.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, A. Institutional and Implementation Arrangements, 2.(c) establish by not laterthan 120 days after the Effective Date and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project, a selectioncommittee for RBGs, with composition, mandate, and terms of reference acceptable to the Association, as further detailed in theProject Operations Manual (the “Regional Block Grant Investment Selection Committee”), which committee shall be responsible forreviewing applications for, and awarding of, RBGs.
Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, B, 1, (b) carry out the Project in accordance with the provision of the ProjectOperations Manual, as discussed and agreed with the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, B, 1, (c) refrain, from materially and/or substantially amending, revising,waiving, voiding, suspending or abrogating, any provision of the Project Operations Manual, whether in whole or in part, withoutthe prior written concurrence of the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, B, 1,(a) prepare, approve and adopt a Project Operations Manual, in a mannerand substance satisfactory to the Association, which manual shall include, inter alia, (i) the details of the Project activitiesincluding results framework and overall budget; (ii) the Project implementation arrangements, including membership and/orcomposition of the Project Steering Committee, Regional Block Grant Investment Selection Committee, and Project Implementation Unitand terms or reference therefor; (iii) the criteria, guidelines and procedures for implementation of the RBGs, including targetingof Eligible RBG Beneficiaries, conditionality requirements and verification protocols therefor, and disbursement of the RBGs; and(iv) the monitoring and evaluation and reporting requirements for the Project.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, C, 1, (a) prepare and adopt by not later than May 1 of each year, an annualwork plan and budget (the “Annual Work Plan and Budget”) for the following fiscal year in a manner, form and substance satisfactoryto the Association, which work plan and budget shall identify the Project activities by component and subcomponent, together withtheir related expenditures and financing sources and, for each such proposed activity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the firstsuch Annual Work Plan and Budget for the first year of Project implementation shall be prepared by SACEP not later than two monthsafter the Effective Date.

comment.narrative: Innovations are defined as new approaches, transfer or adaptation of existing and/or proven approaches to new contexts and/or geographies, new policies, national and regional strategies, standards, etc. It is estimated that approx. 20 grants to be allocated for RBG and that each of these will feature at least one unique innovation that moves toward circularity. Number of innovations is likely to be higher. The indicator measures the PDO outcome on innovations. Cumulative targets.

title.narrative: PDO 2: Policies/standards /guidelines to promote a circular plastic economy harmonized and agreed by at least 3 countries at regional PPP convenings

comment.narrative:
End target achieved.
The following key topics have been addressed/discussed in the RTD sessions. (06 sessions, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Maldives) 1. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), Regulations on single-use plastic phase-outs, 2. Certification and standardization for recycled products, 3. National plastic waste management strategy/action plan and 4. Plastic credit.
The policies, regulations, and standards identified in the national high-level roundtable discussions will be further discussed in the regional high-level roundtable discussion to highlight commonalities across member countries. These will be established as guiding principles to address plastic pollution prevention and management in the South Asia region (SAR). The goal is to identify shared requirements and build consensus among the countries in the region, aiming for the harmonization of policies and practices. The source of this information is from the SACEP PIU team.

title.narrative: PDO 2: Policies/standards /guidelines to promote a circular plastic economy harmonized and agreed by at least 3 countries at regional PPP convenings

comment.narrative:
The project supports a collaboration and coordination arrangement between public and private sectors for jointly addressing plastic pollution. A key result of the convening will be harmonization of policies/standards/guidelines to promote a circular plastic econoy that subsequently facilitate investments. Harmonization opportunities and priorities will be established by the regional PPP convenings and could range from mandatory policies (e.g., plastic bag bans) to voluntary standards (e.g., for plastic products and packaging). Since some countries take a long time to approve policies/standards/guidelines, regional harmonization is considered to be achieved if a majority, i.e., at least 3 participating countries agreed.
The target for number of policies/standards/guidelines harmonized is cumulative.

title.narrative: IR1.5: People reached in plastic pollution and mitigation awareness campaigns (disaggregated by country and sex)

comment.narrative:
During the reporting period, the PLEASE project engaged 114,345 individuals through various activities designed to raise awareness about plastic pollution and its mitigation strategies.
The project held 6 national roundtable discussions, 7 workshops, 6 marine litter consultations, and a regional hackathon, drawing 1,201 participants from a diverse range of sectors, including government, private industry, academia, NGOs, UN entities, CBOs, youth groups, innovators, and fishing communities.
Additionally, awareness sessions led by grantees focused on plastic waste management, including collection, segregation, recycling, and circular plastic economy practices. These sessions reached 113,144 individuals across the region, including school children, youth, women, university students, informal waste workers, recyclers, entrepreneurs, community leaders, members of womenâ€™s and local organizations and NGOs, policymakers, local authorities, vulnerable groups and general public.

title.narrative: IR1.4: Regional circular plastic economy innovations knowledge sharing hosted by SACEP operational

comment.narrative: End target achieved. The PLEASE project has developed and operationalized regional-level knowledge sharing on circular plastic economy innovations. This has been accomplished through six national high-level roundtable discussions ( 04 in the reporting year) , seven workshops ( 05 in the reporting year) , and active participation in annual global and regional conferences such as the INC and COP . The project also organized a side event at INC-5, focusing on grant knowledge sharing under the thematic areas: innovation, decent jobs and inclusion. Additionally, a TED Talk was delivered at the APFSD 2024. In addition to these in-person engagements, online knowledge sharing has been facilitated through the projectâ€™s website, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, and e-newsletters through-out the reporting period . These digital platforms have provided valuable opportunities for stakeholders to exchange data, best practices, and innovative solutions in the circular plastic economy.
